brief.headline: Samsung +27%, SK Hynix +30% on Record Single-Day Gains After Hyperscaler Earnings Reignite AI Capex Optimism
brief.summary: <cite index="39-7,39-8,39-9">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix posted record single-day gains of nearly 27% and 30% respectively on July 31, tracking a sharp rally in U.S. technology stocks after blockbuster earnings from Amazon and Microsoft revived optimism around AI spending.</cite> <cite index="11-1,16-1,16-2">DRAM contract prices are projected to rise 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026, while NAND Flash contract prices are expected to increase 10-15% QoQ, according to TrendForce.</cite> <cite index="28-5,28-7">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from around 20% currently to about 10% by end-2026, with monthly capacity reaching 120,000-140,000 wafers in 2026.</cite> <cite index="5-3,5-6">SK Hynix will likely secure a largely stable market share in the HBM market in 2026 around 50% of total bits, with HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% to 17.1 billion gigabits.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, followed by Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%.</cite> Given Samsung's ongoing HBM3E qualification struggles versus Hynix's entrenched 50%+ bit-share lock and faster time-to-market on HBM4, maintain overweight Hynix relative to Samsung. <cite index="5-4">Pricing pushback is possible as Samsung inches closer to HBM3E qualification</cite>, which could compress Hynix ASPs modestly but Samsung remains structurally disadvantaged on mix and volume. Today's violent rebound (Hynix +30% vs Samsung +27%) reflects beta-amplified relief rally, not fundamental re-rating.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="17-10">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026, with buyers paying roughly double what they paid three months earlier.</cite> <cite index="11-9,11-10">Demand for AI inference systems and hyperscale data centers remains strong enough to keep both DRAM and NAND supply constrained, while memory manufacturers continue shifting production capacity toward higher-margin server products, leaving less capacity available for consumer memory.</cite> Rate of increase is decelerating but absolute levels remain elevated. Consumer resistance building; <cite index="11-4">higher memory costs are gradually feeding through into retail pricing, a trend TrendForce believes could weigh on PC shipments for the rest of the year.</cite>

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="8-4,8-12">Top three memory makers have already allocated their full HBM output for the year, with Micron guiding for a 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="9-4">SK Hynix reported a five-fold jump in quarterly profit in April and said HBM demand is expected to exceed supply over the next three years.</cite> <cite index="42-28,42-29">SK Hynix began HBM4 mass shipments during Q2 2026, with management planning a larger production ramp.</cite> Capacity fully pre-sold through 2027; Samsung qualification delays on HBM3E create vendor concentration risk for hyperscalers, supporting Hynix pricing power near-term.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung +27%, SK Hynix +30% post record single-day gains on hyperscaler earnings optimism
news_pulse.implication: Violent reversal after multi-day correction; foreign flows + short-covering amplified move. Tests durability of AI capex narrative post-Microsoft/Amazon beats.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI surges 14% in largest one-day jump on record
news_pulse.implication: Extreme volatility signals positioning flush and leveraged ETF rebalancing. Analyst notes 'bipolar' trading pattern; sustainability depends on sustained foreign buying.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex hits $690B in 2026, up 81% YoY with 75% allocated to AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Confirms structural demand tailwind for HBM and enterprise DRAM/NAND through 2027. Wall Street consensus reaching $930B by 2028.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as capacity reaches 120K-140K wafers/month
news_pulse.implication: Easing packaging bottleneck unlocks incremental HBM attach; supports 2H26 AI accelerator shipment ramps for Nvidia Blackwell/Rubin and AMD MI350/MI400.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026, NAND +10-15% per TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: Sequential deceleration from Q1's 93-98% QoQ spike but pricing remains elevated. ADATA citing 20-30% DRAM, 35-40% NAND guidance suggests upside risk to TrendForce midpoint.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix controls 57% HBM revenue share (Q4 2025) vs Samsung 22%, Micron 21%
news_pulse.implication: Hynix market dominance intact despite Samsung HBM3E progress. Vendor diversification pressure from hyperscalers could modestly erode share in 2H26 if Samsung qualifies.

news_pulse.headline: Memory makers divert capacity to AI as HBM3E consumes 3x wafer area of standard DRAM
news_pulse.implication: Structural tightness in commodity DRAM/NAND persists as fab space reallocated to HBM. PC/mobile memory deprioritized, reinforcing bifurcated pricing by end-market.

news_pulse.headline: UBS: HBM bit shipments to jump 35% to 17.1B Gb in 2026; SK Hynix maintains ~50% market share
news_pulse.implication: Bit growth in-line with hyperscaler GPU ramps. Hynix pricing power sustained despite Samsung/Micron capacity adds; only 'minimal to modest' ASP downtick expected.

brief.derivatives_signal: ADR-to-KRW premia collapsed from ~60% (July 30) to normalized levels post-rally. Implied volatility spike reversed; options market pricing lower near-term dispersion after leveraged ETF unwind. Monitor KOSPI 200 futures for directional conviction—today's +14% index move driven by short-covering and mechanical rebalancing, not sustained repositioning.
